# SystemVerilog refusal register (ls-sv, schema sv-0.2)

This file answers three questions about the SystemVerilog tier of lean-surfaces (ls-sv): **what does it refuse today**,
**what is meant to be allowed later (and what has to exist first)**, and **what will never be allowed (and which principle says so)**.

It is generated from [`docs/sv-refusals.json`](sv-refusals.json) by `tools/gen_sv_refusals.py` and checked against the code by
`python3 tools/gen_sv_refusals.py --check`: a tagged refusal in the extractor or the Lean code that is missing from the data, or a
listed tag that has disappeared from the code, fails the check. The svGolf-facing twin, for contestants and task authors, is
`svgolf/REFUSALS.md`, generated from the same data. It lives with the svGolf project (the golf branch), so the paths under `svgolf/`
cited in this file are absent from a checkout without it.

A refusal is a LOUD `Unsupported` node (extractor) or a loud process / expression / elaboration error (Lean) or a loader gate: the
design either loads with a defined meaning or it does not load. Nothing here is silently approximated. The long reasons live in the
per-topic documents linked at the end (`docs/sv-*.md`); this register is the index and the classification.

Register of the sv-0.2 SYMBOLIC tier: `extractors/sv/extract.py` in symbolic mode (the `load_design_sv2` path), the Lean side (`LeanModels/Sv`: Param2, Hier2, Ingest2, Probe2, RangeGuard2, CombGuard2, CombAlias2, Sem2, Comb2Proc, the `sv_structure` recognizer), and the loader gates. The svGolf checker's own restrictions are in `svgolf/REFUSALS.md` (the svGolf project, golf branch), generated from the same data. Snapshot: working tree of branch `svgolf-prep` on 2026-10-29, including the uncommitted round-6 work (`PortConn:net-width`, `ArraySel:partial-overhang`, `Select:partial-overhang`, `Select:wide-index`, `AlwaysComb:alias-read`); regenerate after the in-flight jobs land.

## How to read this register

Every construct the sv-0.2 tier does not accept is refused LOUDLY, never evaluated to a guess. Each row is one refusal tag (or a family of tags) with a measured trigger, the reason, where the code raises it, and its future. Marks: `†` = proposed by the register authors, not yet confirmed by Thomas; `(unverified)` = read from the source, not triggered by a run; a bare category without `†` is a recorded decision or a plain statement of today's behaviour.

### The four categories

| category | meaning |
|---|---|
| `refused-now` | refused loudly today and this is the intended behaviour at this version; no future is recorded |
| `later` | refused today and intended to be ALLOWED once a stated prerequisite is met (a proof obligation, a model extension, a checker stage, a measured benefit); the row names the prerequisite and, where recorded, the plan item |
| `never` | refused by principle and not to be allowed: no meaning can be given that is the same for the proof (ls-sv / slang) and the score (Yosys netlist), or it is not synthesizable hardware, or it would let the proved design differ from the scored one; the row names the principle |
| `refused-pending` | decided and in flight, not yet in the code (transitional): the row names the decision; the completeness check allows its tag to be absent and warns once it appears |

### Two scopes: the ls-sv tier and svGolf admission

The register classifies each refusal for the **ls-sv semantics tier** (the `category` of the row). The charter rules the tier's endgame to be
the whole specification, including the verification tier (classes, constrained randomization, assertions) and the full clause-4 scheduler
([docs/sv-charter.md](sv-charter.md) sections 6.3, 6.4, 6.6), so a construct can be `later` for ls-sv and still be unacceptable in a
**svGolf submission**, whose scored artifact is a combinational Yosys netlist. Where the two differ the row carries a second line
`svGolf: ...` (the field `svgolf` in the data). Delays, randomness, classes, strings and reals are the typical cases: `later` in the
semantics, `never` for a golf submission (principles `P-NO-TIME`, `P-SYNTHESIZABLE`).

### Principles behind `never`

| principle | statement |
|---|---|
| `P-SAME-PROGRAM` | Proof and score read ONE program: a construct the two frontends (slang for the proof, Yosys for the score) read differently, that slang rejects, or that Yosys cannot read, cannot be admitted. |
| `P-NO-TOOL-DIRECTIVES` | No construct whose meaning is a synthesis-tool directive: pragmas, attributes, `ifdef SYNTHESIS / YOSYS, translate_off comments. |
| `P-NO-TIME` | No delays, timing, wall-clock or time-dependent behaviour in a combinational task: synthesis ignores them, so the proved (timed) behaviour and the scored netlist would differ. |
| `P-SYNTHESIZABLE` | Not synthesizable hardware: classes, dynamic memory, strings, reals, file I/O, fork/join, program blocks, DPI; the scored artifact is a Yosys gate netlist. |
| `P-NO-SILENT-PICK` | The tools split (Icarus, Xcelium, Verilator, Yosys, slang give different values for the same text) and no consistent reading exists: refuse loudly, never decide for one side. |
| `P-DETERMINISM` | Nondeterministic or scheduling-dependent results: a combinational result must be a function of the inputs, whatever the schedule. |
| `P-TRUSTED-BASE` | (added by the register authors, to confirm) The evidence a verdict rests on (checker, trusted statement, generated Goal, axiom set, toolchain) must not be changeable by the submission; a proof is accepted by the kernel from the allowed axioms alone. |

## The register

One section per group. Columns: tag, a measured trigger (`H:` = the body of `module t(input logic [7:0] a, b, input logic c, output logic [7:0] y); ... endmodule`), why, where the code raises it (`file:function`; `python3 tools/gen_sv_refusals.py --where ID` prints current line numbers), and the status.

### Procedural statements

Loops, waits, disables, assignments in odd positions, local declarations. The extractor tags that are slang class names (`ForLoopStatement`, ...) are the symbolic tier's default tag for a statement it has no lowering for.

| tag | trigger | why | where | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ForLoopStatement` | H: always_comb begin y=0; for (int i=0;i<4;i++) y[i]=a[i]; end | No procedural-loop semantics in the symbolic tier; needs a bounded unroll or an induction rule per parameter point. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: loop semantics in Sem2 / Comb2Proc (elaboration-time unroll of statically bounded loops), driven by the popcount task [LOOPS] |
| `WhileLoopStatement / DoWhileLoopStatement` | H: always_comb begin int i; y=0; i=0; while (i<4) begin y[i]=a[i]; i=i+1; end end (and do..while) | Same as for loops; a data-dependent trip count is additionally not combinational hardware. | `extract.py:_convert_test_loop` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: as ForLoopStatement, statically bounded forms only [LOOPS] |
| `RepeatLoopStatement` | H: always_comb begin y=0; repeat (2) y = y + a; end | No loop semantics in the symbolic tier. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: as ForLoopStatement, constant repeat count [LOOPS] |
| `ForeverLoopStatement` | H: initial forever #5 y = a; | A non-terminating process is a time construct, not combinational logic. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **later**: the full scheduler (initial, # delays) of ruling 6.4 [R1]<br>svGolf: **never**† P-NO-TIME |
| `ForeachLoopStatement` | H: logic [3:0] m [0:3]; always_comb begin y=0; foreach (m[i]) m[i]=a[3:0]; y=m[0]; end | Iteration over unpacked arrays; no loop semantics in the symbolic tier. | `extract.py:_convert_foreach_loop` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: loop semantics plus run-time-indexed unpacked arrays (AGGR) [LOOPS] |
| `WaitStatement` | H: initial begin wait (c) y = a; end | Level-sensitive wait is a time / scheduling construct. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **later**: the scheduler (R1) [R1]<br>svGolf: **never**† P-NO-TIME |
| `DisableStatement` | H: always_comb begin : blk y=a; disable blk; end | Early exit from a named block needs control flow the Sem2 statement model does not have. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: an early-exit (named block / disable) control-flow model in the Sem2 statement model |
| `EventTriggerStatement` | H: event e; always_comb begin y=a; -> e; end | Named events are simulation synchronisation objects. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **later**: the scheduler (R1): events are region objects [R1]<br>svGolf: **never**† P-SYNTHESIZABLE |
| `RandCaseStatement` | H: always_comb begin randcase 1: y=a; 1: y=b; endcase end | Randomised branch choice: not deterministic hardware. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **later**: constrained randomization of the verification tier [VERIF]<br>svGolf: **never**† P-DETERMINISM |
| `PatternCaseStatement` | H: always_comb begin case (a) matches 8'd1: y=1; default: y=0; endcase end | Tagged-union / pattern matching has no model in Sem2; whether Yosys reads tagged-union patterns was not established. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: tagged unions in the symbolic tier [AGGR] |
| `ConditionalStatement:Unique \| :Unique0 \| :Priority` | H: always_comb begin unique if (c) y=a; else y=b; end (unique0, priority likewise) | Yosys reads the qualifiers as full_case / parallel_case don't-cares, so a violated claim scores 0 GE; v0 refuses and WP5 will encode the claim as a proof obligation. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **later**: WP5: a violated unique / unique0 / priority claim becomes a run-time error on the settled state, forced by Terminates2 [WP5] |
| `ConditionalStatement:multi \| :pattern, ConditionalExpression:multi \| :pattern \| :union-shape` | H: always_comb begin if (c &&& b[0]) y=1; else y=0; end / if (a matches 8'd1) ... | &&& conditions and `matches` patterns belong to tagged-union pattern matching, not modelled. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt`, `extract.py:_convert_conditional_expr` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: tagged unions in the symbolic tier [AGGR] (unverified) |
| `CaseStatement:WildcardJustZ (casez)` | H: always_comb begin casez (a) 8'b1???_????: y=1; default: y=0; endcase end | Wildcard case matching is not in Sem2's case model (normal and inside only); wildcard digits interact with the fourstate stage. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: wildcard case semantics in Sem2 plus a fourstate rule for wildcard digits [CASEFEAT] |
| `CaseStatement:WildcardXOrZ (casex)` | H: always_comb begin casex (a) 8'b1xxx_xxxx: y=1; default: y=0; endcase end | As casez, and an x in the SELECTOR also becomes a wildcard, which is the hazardous reading. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: as casez; item-only wildcard use first [CASEFEAT] |
| `AssignmentExpression:compound` | H: always_comb begin y=a; y += b; end | Read-modify-write desugaring exists only on the M0 path. | `extract.py:_convert_compound_assignment` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: symbolic read-modify-write lowering (sizes and signedness per point) [OPS] |
| `ExpressionStatement:UnaryExpression-target \| -type` | H: logic [7:0] m [0:1]; always_comb begin y=a; m[0]=0; m[a[0]]++; end | ++ / -- only on a plain integral identifier. | `extract.py:_convert_incdec` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: select targets for ++ / -- [OPS] |
| `AssignmentExpression (assignment used as an expression)` | H: always_comb begin y = (a = b); end | An assignment inside an expression is a side effect in expression position. | `extract.py:_convert_expr`, `extract.py:_convert_assignment_expr` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: expression-level side effects [OPS] |
| `AssignmentExpression:target` | H: logic [7:0] m [0:3]; always_comb begin m[k]=a; ... end / always_comb {y,z}=a; / y[b[2:0] +: 2] = ... | The target is not an identifier, constant select or admitted concatenation leaf set; a split RHS needs a single sample and disjoint windows. | `extract.py:_convert_assignment_expr`, `extract.py:convert_continuous_assign` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: run-time-indexed targets and general concatenation targets in Sem2 [SELFEAT] |
| `AssignmentExpression:target (overlapping continuous drivers)` | H: assign y = a; assign y = b; / assign y[3:0]=a[3:0]; assign y[5:2]=b[3:0]; | Two continuous drivers on overlapping bits of a net: the one-driver rule (F3) refuses; resolution functions are not modelled. | `extract.py:_reject_overlapping_symbolic_drivers` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: a resolved-net / strength model (the Yosys netlist would also have to resolve) [NETRES] |
| `AssignmentExpression:selected-effects` | a select-target assignment whose RHS has effects | A selected-target assignment needs an effect-free RHS so the single-sample rule holds. | `extract.py:_convert_assignment_expr` | **refused-now** (unverified) |
| `IntraAssignment:publication-or-context` | H: always_comb begin y = #1 a; end / always_ff @(posedge c) y <= #1 a; | Intra-assignment delays are time constructs. | `extract.py:_convert_intra_assignment` | **later**: the scheduler (R1) [R1]<br>svGolf: **never**† P-NO-TIME |
| `InvalidStatement` | H: always_comb begin y = zzz; end (undefined name; also `a == b;` as a statement) | slang marks a statement it rejected as bad; the extractor continues after frontend errors, so the bad node stays loud. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **never**†: P-SAME-PROGRAM |
| `ImmediateAssertion:symbolic` | H: always_comb begin y=a; assert (c); end / assert #0 (c); | Assertions (with action blocks that print) have no symbolic-tier semantics. | `extract.py:_convert_immediate_assertion` | **later**: assertions of the verification tier [VERIF] |
| `Scanf:assignment-context` | H: int n, v; always_comb begin y=a; n = $sscanf("12","%d",v); end | String / file formatted input; M0 handles only literal forms. | `extract.py:_convert_scan_assignment` | **later**: strings and formatted input of the verification tier [VERIF]<br>svGolf: **never**† P-SYNTHESIZABLE |
| `BlockStatement:JoinAll \| :JoinAny \| :JoinNone` | H: initial begin fork y = a; join end (join_none likewise) | fork / join: parallel processes with scheduling-dependent results. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **later**: the scheduler (R1) with the determinism boundary [R1]<br>svGolf: **never**† P-SYNTHESIZABLE |
| `VariableDeclStatement:2state \| :type \| :signed` | H: always_comb begin real r; y=a; end / logic [7:0] m [0:1]; as a block-local | Block-local declarations of non-4-state or non-packed types (block-local packed 4-state variables are admitted by the extractor, see loader gates). | `extract.py:_convert_local_decl` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: 2-state declared types and unpacked arrays in the symbolic tier [AGGR]<br>svGolf: **never**† P-SYNTHESIZABLE |
| `ContinuousAssignSymbol:form` | a malformed continuous assign (not isolated) | Defensive. | `extract.py:convert_continuous_assign` | **refused-now** (unverified) |
| `<expr>:target-source \| :target-index \| :target-operand \| :target-selection \| :target-type` | a streaming-concatenation or select target the legacy blocking-target lowering cannot express | The target shape is outside the admitted select / concat leaf set. | `extract.py:legacy_blocking_target`, `extract.py:_streaming_target_assignment` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: general target shapes (see AssignmentExpression:target) [SELFEAT] (unverified) |
| `Case:inside-width` | case (a) inside 4: ... where an item is wider than the subject at the instantiated point | case...inside compares pairwise (==?); one common width is exact only if no item is wider; there is no Icarus oracle for the construct. | `Param2.lean:instStmt2` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: pairwise inside comparison at differing widths plus an oracle that runs the construct [CASEFEAT] |
| `AssignL (an assignment target that does not lower)` | undeclared target, negative constant index, bad part-select bounds, nested or empty concatenation target, a leaf that overhangs its vector, dynamic indexed part-select target | The write window cannot be fixed; concat targets must write exactly each leaf's declared width or the split of the RHS would shift. | `Param2.lean:instStmt2`, `Param2.lean:instProcess2`, `Param2.lean:instLhsLeaf2`, `Param2.lean:instLhs2` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: nested concat targets and window clipping with a recorded reading [SELFEAT] (unverified) |
| `Assign (target not a declared signal at this point)` | a generate body declaring `logic t` then `assign t = a[i]` (the target is an undeclared module-level name) | Per-instance scoping of generate-local declarations is not modelled. | `Param2.lean:instProcess2` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: generate-local declaration scoping (see GenerateDecl) |

### Processes, event controls and always blocks

| tag | trigger | why | where | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TimedStatement:DelayControl` | H: initial begin #1 y = a; end (inside always_comb the source is a slang error: InvalidStatement) | Delays are time. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt`, `extract.py:convert_procedural_block` | **later**: the scheduler (R1) [R1]<br>svGolf: **never**† P-NO-TIME |
| `TimedStatement:SignalEventControl (second wait inside a process)` | H: always_ff @(posedge c) begin y <= a; @(posedge c) y <= b; end | A second event wait inside a process is a multi-cycle sequential process. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **later**: the sequential layer [SEQ] |
| `TimedStatement:EventListControl` | H: always @(a or b) y = a; / always_ff @(posedge clk or posedge rst) ... / a three-event list | Plain `always` lists with one or more edge-qualified 1-bit identifiers are modelled by the retained timed event-list process; scalar identifier, equality/inequality, and logical `iff` guards are sampled at publication, while empty, unsupported-conditional, non-scalar, `always_ff`, and three-event clock/reset forms remain loud. | `extract.py:convert_procedural_block` | **later**: the sequential layer (generic sensitivity lists) [SEQ] |
| `TimedStatement:ImplicitEventControl (always @*)` | H: always @* y = a; | A level-sensitive block that can infer a latch with no proc error in Yosys; its initial-x behaviour differs between tools. | `extract.py:convert_procedural_block` | **later**: a 4-state rule for the initial x of a level-sensitive block in score/fourstate.py before ls-sv runs it [LATCH4] |
| `SignalEventControl:BothEdges \| :None_` | H: always_ff @(edge c) y <= a; / always_ff @(c) / always @(c) ... | Plain timed `always @(signal)` is modelled through the retained any-edge registration; `always_ff @(signal)` and both-edge controls still lack the clocked edge contract. | `extract.py:convert_procedural_block`, `extract.py:_convert_event_wait` | **later**: the sequential layer [SEQ] |
| `SignalEventControl:iff` | H: always_ff @(posedge c iff b[0]) y <= a; | Plain timed `always`, positive- or negative-edge `always_ff` clocks, and the clock event of a two-edge asynchronous-reset `always_ff` admit scalar identifier, equality/inequality, and logical `iff` guards and sample them when the adjacent edge is published; unsupported guards and guards placed on the reset event remain loud. | `extract.py:convert_procedural_block` | **later**: the sequential layer [SEQ] |
| `SignalEventControl:iff-reset` | H: always_ff @(posedge c or negedge rst_n iff en) y <= a; | A scalar `iff` guard is admitted on the clock event of an asynchronous-reset list, but the reset event is unconditional. Guarding the reset edge needs a separate reset qualification rule and remains loud. | `extract.py:_sym_areset_process` | **later**: the sequential layer [SEQ] |
| `SignalEventControl:clock` | H: always_ff @(posedge a) y <= b; (8-bit clock) | The clock must be a 1-bit identifier; the envelope has no sampled-value register for the LSB rule. | `extract.py:convert_procedural_block` | **later**: the sequential layer [SEQ] |
| `ProceduralBlockSymbol:NoEventControl (zero-delay always)` | H: always y = a; / always_ff y <= a; | A zero-delay `always` without event control never yields: a non-terminating process. | `extract.py:convert_procedural_block` | **never**†: P-DETERMINISM |
| `ProceduralBlockSymbol:NoEventControl (concurrent assertion)` | module-level `assert property (...)` or `cover property (...)` (slang reports them as procedural blocks) | Concurrent assertions have no process model. | `extract.py:convert_procedural_block` | **later**: assertions of the verification tier [VERIF] |
| `ProceduralBlockSymbol:AlwaysLatch` | H: always_latch if (c) y = a; | A latch's initial value is x in IEEE but Yosys resolves a never-loaded latch to 0 (measured), so a 4-state rule is needed first. | `extract.py:convert_procedural_block` | **later**: a 4-state rule for a latch's initial x in score/fourstate.py before ls-sv models always_latch [LATCH4] |
| `ProceduralBlockSymbol:Final` | H: final $display("x"); | final blocks run at simulation end only. | `extract.py:convert_procedural_block` | **later**: the scheduler (R1) [R1]<br>svGolf: **never**† P-SYNTHESIZABLE |
| `ProceduralBlockSymbol:initialized-variable \| :initialized-unknown` | logic [7:0] q = 8'd1; always_comb q = a; (also always_ff writing q) | The initializer counts as a procedural write (LRM 6.5, 10.5): Xcelium rejects the design (MULAXX) where Icarus, Yosys and slang run it. The common FPGA idiom `logic q = 0; always_ff ... q <= ...` is refused too (a recorded over-refusal). | `extract.py:convert_procedural_block` | **never**: P-NO-SILENT-PICK |

### Expressions and operators

| tag | trigger | why | where | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `UnaryExpression:Preincrement \| :Postincrement \| :Predecrement \| :Postdecrement` | H: logic [7:0] k; always_comb begin k=a; y=(k++); end | Side-effecting operators inside expressions are not modelled (statement-position `y++;` is admitted and lowered to a blocking assignment). | `extract.py:_convert_unary_expr` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: expression-level side effects [OPS] |
| `InsideExpression, ValueRangeExpression` | H: assign y = (a inside {1,2,3}) ? a : b; / case (a) inside 8'd1, [8'd3:8'd5]: ... | The `inside` operator and range items [lo:hi] are lowered only in the M0 path; plain `case inside` items are admitted. | `extract.py:_convert_expr` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: range patterns in PStmt.caseStmt / Expr2 and a symbolic lowering of `inside` [CASEFEAT] |
| `HierarchicalValueExpression` | a child instance output read as `u.y`; a generate-block signal `g[7].w`; an interface member `i.d` | Hierarchical references are not modelled. | `extract.py:_convert_expr` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: hierarchical names in Hier2 flattening [HIERFEAT] |
| `SimpleAssignmentPatternExpression \| StructuredAssignmentPatternExpression \| ReplicatedAssignmentPatternExpression` | logic [7:0] k; assign k = '{default: 1'b1}; / parameter int A[2] = '{1,2} | Assignment patterns are lowered only in the M0 path. | `extract.py:_convert_expr` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: symbolic assignment patterns (default:, keyed, replicated) [AGGR] |
| `BinaryExpression:BinaryXnor` | H: parameter Q = (6 ~^ 3); / localparam logic [3:0] M = 4'b1010 ~^ 4'b0110; / if ((i ~^ 1) != 0) in a generate (every symbolic-CONSTANT position) | The binary XNOR `~^` (and its spelling `^~`, one slang operator) is SUPPORTED in signal expressions of the symbolic tier since WP-L2 (2026-10-30): the extractor lowers it to `~(a ^ b)`, so any x/z operand bit gives x and equal known bits give 1 (IEEE 1800-2023 Table 11-14), at the expression's own context width and signedness. It stays loud in a parameter default, a localparam or a generate condition: the constant tier has its own width rules for `~` (an INT-class `~` is refused there) and the lowering was not measured against them. | `extract.py:_convert_binary_expr`, `extract.py:_convert_xnor_expr` | **later**: a measured width rule for `~` / `^` in the constant tier (Param.lean `evalInt` refuses an INT-class `~`; `evalSized` has the sized case), then the same lowering in constant positions |
| `BinaryExpression:LogicalEquivalence` | H: assign y = c <-> b[0]; | Operator absent from BINARY_OPS (implication `->` is handled separately). | `extract.py:_convert_binary_expr` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: operator set extension [OPS] |
| `BinaryExpression:Divide-type \| :Mod-type \| :Power-type \| :Shift-type` | H: assign y = a / 1.5; a ** 1.5 | Non-integral operand of a division, modulo, power or shift (the node is replaced by the enclosing ConversionExpression:width, so the tag may never reach the envelope). | `extract.py:_convert_binary_expr` | **later**: reals of the verification tier [VERIF]<br>svGolf: **never**† P-SYNTHESIZABLE (unverified) |
| `BinaryExpression:width \| :signedness, UnaryExpression:width, ConditionalExpression:width, ConcatenationExpression:width, LogicalImplication:source \| :operand, CallExpression:arity \| :cast-width, SigningCast:signature` | internal width / signedness / arity consistency guards (no source found that reaches them) | Defensive: a converted operand whose width disagrees with slang's would silently change the value. | `extract.py:_convert_binary_expr`, `extract.py:_convert_unary_expr`, `extract.py:_convert_conditional_expr`, `extract.py:_convert_concat_expr`, `extract.py:_convert_implication_expr`, `extract.py:_sym_cast_call` | **refused-now** (unverified) |
| `CallExpression:dimension:* ($left, $right, $low, $high, ...)` | H: (N parametric) always_comb begin y=a; void'($left(a)); end | Dimension queries of a range that moves with the parameter fold the default point; only $high / $size of a declared signal are carried per point. | `extract.py:_convert_dimension_query` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: per-point dimension queries [FOLDS] |
| `CallExpression:$clog2:signature \| :arity \| :argument` | malformed $clog2 call | Defensive argument checks of the $clog2 lowering. | `extract.py:_convert_sym_call_expr` | **refused-now** (unverified) |
| `InvalidExpression, ContinuousAssignSymbol:InvalidExpression, PortConnection:InvalidExpression` | H: assign y = zzz; / child output connected to y[k] with a run-time k | Frontend-rejected expression kept loud. | `extract.py:_convert_expr`, `extract.py:convert_continuous_assign`, `extract.py:_sym_port_conn` | **never**†: P-SAME-PROGRAM |

| `generate if: <err>` | a generate-if condition whose constant evaluation fails (defensive: slang requires a constant) | The branch taken cannot be decided at elaboration. | `Hier2.lean:GenItem.expandH`, `Param2.lean:GenItem.expand2` | **refused-now** (unverified) |
| `generate for: <err>, generate step outside the ++/-- tier` | a generate-for whose init fails constant evaluation or whose step is not `g++` / `g--` of the loop genvar (the extractor emits only those) | The genvar sequence cannot be computed by genvarSeq. | `Hier2.lean:GenItem.expandH`, `Param2.lean:GenItem.expand2`, `Param.lean:stepDelta` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: more step forms (g += k) in stepDelta; today defensive (unverified) |

A parameter amount is never folded to 1 (it is folded at the default point only), and an unsigned or narrower literal changes the arithmetic type of `g - 1`. | `extract.py:_genstep`, `extract.py:_genstep_delta` | **later**: a general constant step (an amount, either sign, evaluated per point) in stepDelta / genvarSeq and in the tactics' step pattern |

| `GenerateDecl:<kind>` | a Var, Net, LocalParam or ParameterDecl inside a generate body: for (genvar i...) begin : g logic t; localparam int K = i+1; ... end | Generate-local declarations need per-instance scoping and hoisting; a loud item, not an envelope parse failure. | `Ingest2.lean:parseGenItem` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: hoist generate-local declarations as `<path>.<name>` like instance signals (Hier2 already hoists) |

### Parameters, constants and default-point folds

slang folds many constants at the DEFAULT parameter point; emitting that fold would be silently wrong at other points, so the extractor and the Lean constant tier refuse the shapes where default-point and per-point values can differ (the FOLDS lane, [docs/sv-charter.md](sv-charter.md) rounds 3 to 7).

| tag | trigger | why | where | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `EnumValueSymbol:default-point-value \| :unsized-literal-member` | an enum whose member values depend on a parameter, or unsized-literal members, used as a value | Member values are slang's default-point constants. | `extract.py:_sym_named_value` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: symbolic enum member values [FOLDS] |
| `VariableSymbol:default-point-array \| :default-point-aggregate` | logic [7:0] mem [0:K-1] with parameter K; a packed struct whose member width names a parameter | The layout is slang's default-point shape (one decl per default cell, fixed member offsets). | `extract.py:convert_var_sym` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: parametric aggregate layout [AGGR] |
| `Syntax:<SyntaxKind> \| Syntax:Identifier:<SymbolClass> \| Syntax:Identifier:unresolved` | a packed dimension recovered from syntax: [f(N)-1:0] with a user function, [$high(a):0], [$bits(logic[N-1:0])-1:0] | slang folds declared dimensions without keeping a bound expression, so they are re-read from syntax; unsupported syntax degrades to Unsupported with the resolved width kept. | `extract.py:_syntax_unsupported`, `extract.py:_syntax_name` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: richer syntax recovery [FOLDS] |
| `parameter '<p>' has no declared type and its override is not an integer expression` | an override of an UNTYPED child parameter by an expression outside the INT class (`child #(.P(3'd5))`) | The parameter would take the override's type (IEEE 6.20.2); the constant tier carries integers and would lose it. | `Hier2.lean:PInst.given` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: typed override values (a type with each override) in PInst.given / atPoint [FOLDS] (unverified) |
| `parameter '<p>' has no default` | a parameter without a default at a point that does not override it; a default whose evaluation fails (`parameter logic [3:0] P = 4'bx01x`) | slang cannot elaborate such a module alone; there is no default point to fix the instantiation. | `Param.lean:PDesign.atPoint`, `Param.lean:PDesign.defaultArgs` | **refused-now** |
| `parameter arity: got <n>, want <m>` | instantiate called with a different number of arguments than the design has parameters (API misuse) | Positional binding would shift every value. | `Param2.lean:instantiate2From`, `Hier2.lean:PDesign.instantiateRec` | **refused-now** (unverified) |
| `parameter '<n>' type: <err>` | a typed parameter whose type width fails (unknown type name, unrecoverable packed dimensions, non-evaluable bounds), or a parameter-dependent type without its signedness | The bound value cannot be converted to a declared type that cannot be sized. | `Param2.lean:instantiate2From`, `Hier2.lean:paramEnvH`, `Param.lean:bindParams` | **refused-now** (unverified) |
| `Constant:context` | a constant subexpression whose evaluation AT the operation width fails (e.g. a division by zero that appears only at the wider width) | The folded value would be wrong at that width. | `Param2.lean:constAtCtx2` | **refused-now** (unverified) |
| `ParamRef:override-type` | a value-position read of an UNTYPED parameter whose default has another type than an int, at a point where an integer override retypes it (IEEE 6.20.2) | The envelope's value-tier tree was typed at the default's type, not the override's. | `Param2.lean:instExpr2`, `Param2.lean:staleMsg2` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: per-point typed trees (probe re-extraction at the point) or retyping in the value tier [FOLDS] |
| `ParamRef:package` | a package-scoped parameter reference `pkg::P` | No package parameter table in IEnv. | `Param2.lean:instExpr2` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: package parameter / enum tables in IEnv (unverified) |
| `ParamRef:unbound \| GenvarRef:unbound \| EnumRef:unknown` | a parameter, genvar or enum member with no binding at this point (a genvar outside its loop; an enum member of an unbound type or from a package) | A name with no value cannot be materialized; defensive for the first two. | `Param2.lean:instExpr2` | **refused-now** (unverified) |
| `<op> in a constant context (division by zero, negative shift, ** exponent above 4096, width-dependent ~ and >>)` | division / modulo by zero; a negative right operand; `'**'` above 4096; `'>>'` of a negative constant; `~` or a bitwise op on a negative constant; vector operators | The constant tier is exact integer arithmetic; a result that would be x, depends on an unknown width or exceeds the bound is refused instead of guessed. | `Param.lean:constArith`, `Param.lean:constShift`, `Param.lean:evalAt` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: width-exact INT-class evaluation for ~, signed shifts and bitwise ops on negatives (division by zero stays refused: the value is x) [FOLDS] (unverified) |
| `<x> in a constant context (signal, x/z literal, concatenation, replication, reduction, unbased-unsized literal)` | a parameter default, localparam, generate bound, dimension bound, select label or override containing a signal, an x/z literal, a concatenation, a replication, a reduction or a fill | Elaboration constants must be known integers; signals are run-time values; x/z literals and width-dependent forms have no integer value here. | `Param.lean:ctype`, `Param.lean:evalAt`, `Param.lean:evalInt` | **later**: x/z constants need the x-taint feature; concatenation / replication / reduction in constants need vector-valued constant folding (a proposal) [XTAINT] (unverified) |

The tools split. | `Param.lean:evalSized`, `Param.lean:assignCtxMsg`, `Param.lean:assignFitMsg` | **refused-now** |
| `Constant:untyped-width` | an UNTYPED parameter default or localparam built with + - * ** or a left shift (`localparam Y = SB + 1'b1;`, `localparam K = N + 1;`), at every point | slang and Yosys give the constant its expression's own type (6.20.2); Icarus 12.0 gives it the LOSSLESS width: different constants wherever the width is observable. A whole-class over-refusal (34 rows). | `Param.lean:evalUntyped`, `Param.lean:untypedWidthMsg`, `Param.lean:PExpr.icarusWidens` | **refused-now** |
| `Constant:untyped-overflow` | an untyped constant whose own-width value differs from its value at 64 more bits (e.g. unary ~ or - on an unsigned value) | slang / Yosys keep the wrapped self-determined value, Icarus evaluates losslessly. The tools split. | `Param.lean:evalUntyped`, `Param.lean:untypedWrapMsg` | **refused-now** (unverified) |
| `localparam '<n>': <err> / enum member bad bits` | a localparam, enum base or enum member that fails constant evaluation or has bad bits | Inherits the constant-tier errors. | `Param.lean:bindLocals`, `Param.lean:checkLocals`, `Param.lean:bindEnums` | **refused-now** (unverified) |

### always_comb guards and the settle semantics

| tag | trigger | why | where | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AlwaysComb:self-read` | H: always_comb begin y = t; t = a; end / if (c) t = a; y = t; t = b; (a bit read before it is written, written later) | IEEE 9.2.2.2.1 leaves variables the block writes out of its sensitivity list: Icarus 12 and Xcelium keep the previous run's value, Verilator and the Yosys netlist give the settled one. The proof and the score would read different programs. | `CombGuard2.lean:combGuardProc`, `CombGuard2.lean:selfReadMsg`, `Param2.lean:instProcess2`, `Hier2.lean:Process2.inInstance`, `Ingest2.lean:load_design_sv2` | **never**: P-NO-SILENT-PICK |
| `AlwaysComb:alias-read` | H: assign w = t; always_comb begin y = w; t = a; end (also assign chains, ~ and slice copies, port loops formed after flattening) | An always_comb reads a bit downstream, through a continuous assign, of a bit it writes at or after the read: Icarus propagates the copy inside the block's run and loses the wake-up (y lags); Xcelium, Verilator and the settle semantics defer it (y = a). The tools split. | `CombAlias2.lean:aliasGuardProc`, `CombAlias2.lean:Design2.aliasGuard`, `CombAlias2.lean:PDesign.aliasReport`, `Ingest2.lean:load_design_sv2`, `runner2.lean:main` | **never**: P-NO-SILENT-PICK |
| `Clock:source` | H: logic clk; always_ff @(posedge clk) y <= a & b; (undriven) / assign clk = 1'b0; ... (tied) / assign g = clk & en; always_ff @(posedge g) ... (gated) / always_ff @(posedge div) with div a register / a clock that is an output or an internal net | Sem2 runs every edge process once per cycle and never reads the clock's value, so it is exact only when the clock is a one-bit INPUT port of the top whose edge is the cycle. A dead, tied, gated, derived, register or internal-net clock captures every cycle in the model and never (or only on enabled edges) in a simulator: measured on Xcelium 24.03 and Icarus 12.0 (rows clk_undriven, clk_tied, clk_gated, clk_internal, clk_reg). | `ClockGuard2.lean:Design2.clockSourceViol`, `ClockGuard2.lean:Design2.clockViolation`, `ClockGuard2.lean:Design2.disciplineGuard`, `ClockGuard2.lean:PDesign.clockReport`, `Ingest2.lean:load_design_sv2`, `runner2.lean:main` | **later**: clock edges as events (S5): edge detection from the clock signal between snapshots, clock gating, derived clocks (a clock produced by NBA logic also needs the R1 slot loop) [SEQ] |
| `Clock:reset` | H: logic rst_q; always_ff @(posedge clk) rst_q <= ~rst; always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_q) ... / @(posedge c or negedge c) / a signal that is both a clock and a reset | An asynchronous reset must be an input port: a reset the design generates is a real asynchronous event in hardware but only a value at a snapshot in the cycle semantics (the reset-event phase compares the settled inputs between snapshots). Measured (row clk_rst_int): simulators reset at the first posedge and hold q = 0, the model gives 1 0 0 1 0. | `ClockGuard2.lean:Design2.clockResetViol`, `ClockGuard2.lean:Design2.clockViolation`, `ClockGuard2.lean:Design2.disciplineGuard`, `ClockGuard2.lean:PDesign.clockReport`, `Ingest2.lean:load_design_sv2`, `runner2.lean:main` | **later**: clock edges as events (S5): an internally generated reset is an event of the active/NBA region, needing edge detection on arbitrary signals [SEQ] |
| `Clock:multiple` | H: always_ff @(posedge clk1) a <= d; always_ff @(posedge clk2) b <= a; (two clock ports) | The cycle step ticks every edge process once, i.e. all clocks together, which no stimulus of a real simulator is bound to do; independent or interleaved clocks need tick sets and interleavings (zero-skew coincident edges sample OLD values, pinned on Xcelium: clk2). | `ClockGuard2.lean:Design2.clockMultiViol`, `ClockGuard2.lean:Design2.clockViolation`, `ClockGuard2.lean:Design2.disciplineGuard`, `ClockGuard2.lean:PDesign.clockReport`, `Ingest2.lean:load_design_sv2`, `runner2.lean:main` | **later**: several clocks (S6): a step is a set of clocks that rise together, the stimulus quantifies all interleavings [SEQ] |
| `Clock:data-read` | H: assign y = clk ^ a; / if (clk) ... / assign ck_o = clk; (output) / a child that reads its own clock port as data (assign y = ck & d) | The model never gives the clock a value (the stimulus does not bind it; it is whatever the entry says or x), a simulator sees the waveform: a design that uses the clock as data is a gated or derived clock in disguise. Measured (rows clk_data, clk_out, clk_child_data). The one exemption is the plain copy `assign t = clk` (what a bare instance clock connection flattens to), whose target joins the clock's copy set and is checked in turn; a copy reaching an output port is refused too. | `ClockGuard2.lean:Design2.clockReadViol`, `ClockGuard2.lean:Design2.clockViolation`, `ClockGuard2.lean:Design2.disciplineGuard`, `ClockGuard2.lean:PDesign.clockReport`, `Ingest2.lean:load_design_sv2`, `runner2.lean:main` | **later**: clock edges as events (S5): the clock as a value needs its waveform in the trace [SEQ] |
| `nonblocking assignment to '<n>' inside always_comb is outside the cycle semantics` | always_comb y <= a; | The comb phase has no NBA region; a queued update has no commit point inside the settle loop. Not refused at load: run2 returns unsupported on the first cycle. | `Sem2.lean:runCombProcess2` | **later**: an NBA queue inside the comb settle loop, or a decision to refuse at instantiation like the other guards [SEQ] |
| `run2: timeout (a combinational loop that never settles)` | assign a = ~a; | combSettle2 re-runs processes to a fixpoint within fuel; an oscillation has no value. Settling cycles are accepted by run2 but proofs need an Acyclic certificate. | `Sem2.lean:combSettle2`, `runner2.lean:main` | **never**†: P-DETERMINISM (unverified) |
| `unsupported expression \| statement \| process '<kind>' (run2)` | run2 reaching any Expr2 / Stmt2 / Process2 `.unsupported` node | This is how every extractor Unsupported node and every loud instantiation process surfaces. `load_design_sv2` does NOT refuse a design merely for holding loud nodes; it refuses only the kinds listed under Loader gates. | `Sem2.lean:evalExpr2`, `Pure2.lean:evalPure2`, `Sem2.lean:execStmt2`, `Sem2.lean:runCombProcess2` | **refused-now** |
| `unknown identifier / assignment target / concatenated target requires continuous-assignment execution` | a read or write of a name absent from the state; a NONBLOCKING assign to a concat target | Unreachable after instantiation (defensive), except the NBA-to-concat-target case: the NBA queue has no split of one sampled RHS over statically sized windows. | `Semantics.lean:readSignal`, `Sem2.lean:resolveLhs2`, `Sem2.lean:resolveConcatLhs2` | **later**: concat targets in the NBA queue and dynamic-leaf windows (part of SEQ) [SEQ] (unverified) |

### Proof tooling (sv_structure, lowerComb, x-free fragment)

These are not refusals of a design: they are the edges of the proof automation. A design outside them still loads and can be proved by hand.

| tag | trigger | why | where | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lowerComb: nonblocking / dynamic-index / concat targets, non assign-or-always_comb processes` | y <= a; y[i] = ... with a run-time i; {c, s} = a + b; always_ff processes | Design2.lowerComb returns none, so the always_comb settle theorem does not apply: the lowering needs a static write window per blocking assignment. | `Comb2Proc.lean:Stmt2.symExec`, `Comb2Proc.lean:Lhs2.symWin`, `Comb2Proc.lean:Process2.lowerComb`, `Comb2Proc.lean:Design2.lowerComb` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: dynamic-window and concat-target symbolic execution (no recorded plan); edge processes follow the sequential layer [WINDOWS] (unverified) |
| `lowerComb: window overlap / unsupported node` | a whole read of a partly written signal; a window read that straddles a written window; `y[0] = a; y = b;`; branches writing overlapping but different windows | The symbolic state keeps disjoint windows; these shapes have no single equation per window. | `Comb2Proc.lean:SymState.readWhole`, `Comb2Proc.lean:SymState.write`, `Comb2Proc.lean:Expr2.symSubst` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: windows with partial overlap in the symbolic state [WINDOWS] (unverified) |
| `lowerComb: selfReadFree` | a body whose equations read a window the body itself writes (latches, `y = t; t = a;`) | One run must be its own fixpoint (runCombProcess2_alwaysComb_idem) for the settle theorem to carry over; a different test from CombGuard2, which admits latches. | `Comb2Proc.lean:SymState.selfReadFree`, `Comb2Proc.lean:Process2.lowerComb` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: a window-level rank and latch support in the lowering [WINDOWS] (unverified) |
| `sv_structure: outside the v1 fragment` | declaration initializer, localparams, enums, out-of-tier members, non-affine indexes or bounds, unary / ?: / replication / reduction / arithmetic operators, part-select or concat targets, always_ff / always_latch / always @ processes, an always_comb body outside the first fragment (more than one written window, `case`, a latch (an `if` without `else`), temporaries or default-then-override, `?:` / `!` / `~` / reductions in a body, nonblocking assignment), nested generate loops deeper than two, conditional generate, instances | The v1 recognizer covers the gate-level assign fragment of the adder and array multiplier with affine geometry, and (WP-G, `PDesign.summaryP`) an `always_comb` body that is an if/else tree writing ONE window, whose leaves are right-hand sides of that fragment and whose conditions are gate trees; anything else cannot be summarized soundly. Reported as `sv_structure: outside the supported fragment`, with the site and the reason (e.g. site `g_bit#1`: always_comb statement `case`). | `CombView.lean:PDesign.summary`, `CombView.lean:declOf?`, `CombView.lean:elemAcc?`, `CombView.lean:rdsOf?`, `CombView.lean:hdrOf?`, `CombView.lean:itemOf?`, `CombProc.lean:treeStmt?`, `CombProcSummary.lean:siteOfP?` | **later**: stage-2 lanes: localparams via the parameter stage, deeper arrays, part-select / concat targets, nested loops, instances; arithmetic is a separate lane (sv_equations); always_comb bodies beyond the first fragment: S1b multi-window bodies, S2 `?:` `!` `~` and reductions in bodies, S3 default-then-override and temporaries (svgolf/design/always-comb/README.md) [STAGE2] (unverified) |
| `sv_structure: structural check failed / the goal must be ... / in-range obligation fails` | duplicate declaration names, an undeclared signal, a driven input, loop variables not distinct, a rank that does not decrease at sampled sizes | The decidable hypotheses of comb_view / acyclic_view (checked by `decide +kernel`) and the tactic contract; a failure reports a REAL design or certificate bug with the offending sites. | `CombViewDiag.lean:Summary.structProblems`, `CombViewTactic.lean:runSvStructure` | **refused-now** (unverified) |
| `Expr2.xfWidth = none (x-free knownness theorem)` | an expression with mismatched operand widths, a dynamic index, / % **, signed forms, wildcard equalities, an unsupported node, or an x literal | Outside the x-free fragment the knownness theorem simply does not apply: their Boolean equations are not written yet, or they can produce x from known inputs (division by zero, out-of-range dynamic index). | `CombKnownBits.lean:Expr2.xfWidth` | **later**: extend xfWidth with signed forms, wildcards and dynamic-index guards; x literals need the x-taint feature [XTAINT] (unverified) |

## Declared departures (not refusals)

These are admitted and DIFFER from a simulator on purpose; each is a hash-bound row in `harness/sv/cases2.json`.

| departure | what differs | source |
|---|---|---|
| Run-time-base part select partly out of range | `v[sel +: 4]` with a signal base keeps the LRM value (in-range bits kept, x elsewhere); Xcelium returns all x. Declared as Xcelium-sim oracle_disagreement rows (partsel_dyn*, dyn32_part). Reason for declaring rather than refusing is not stated in the sources (unverified). | svgolf/PLAN.md Round 6; docs/sv-xcelium-audit.md 6.1 item 1, 6.4 |
| Cross-process bit splits | acg_xproc_bits (LRM-legal; Icarus-only departure, stays declared). | docs/sv-xcelium-audit.md 6.1 item 9 |
| Icarus compiler assertions / vvp aborts | Icarus 'unavailable' rows are declared, not refused. | docs/sv-oracle-disagreements.md 'Unavailable oracles' |

## Known holes: admitted today, not refused

A register of refusals cannot list what nobody refuses. These are the shapes the audits found that the tier ADMITS although a tool disagrees; none has been decided.

| hole | what | source |
|---|---|---|
| 32-bit unsigned run-time part-select base | read as signed by the model (dynPartRead32) while Xcelium and the typing rules read it unsigned (8 dyn32 cells). Options: change the value (forbidden in round 6) or refuse. | docs/sv-xcelium-audit.md 6.4 |
| Shift counts wider than 32 bits | Xcelium truncates a shift count silently and nothing refuses it. (Bit-select indexes are refused, Select:wide-index, including the index of a run-time unpacked-array element where the extractor admits one (the lane-A verifier's probe wi_arr), and part-select bases are refused as RangeSelectExpression:dynamic-wide-base.) | docs/sv-xcelium-audit.md 6.4 |
| PortConn:net-width narrower than the verified rule | full-range part-select or constant bit-select of a net actual, signed net, another instance's output net, tri1 formal, the net-collapse effect of a second mismatched connection and the OUTPUT-direction twin are still admitted. | LeanModels/Sv/Hier2.lean docstring; docs/sv-xcelium-audit.md 6.1 item 7 |
| Self-read guard on the M0 family | PDesign.instantiateD (M0) is not covered by the self-read guard (reachable only at a non-default point of a parametric self-reading body). | docs/sv-charter.md WP4 Gaps |
| Cross-process bit splits | acg_xproc_bits, x_dyn, x_child are admitted (LRM-legal, Icarus-only departure; only one is a declared row). | docs/sv-charter.md round 4 |
| Guards beside name.sem | a forall-N proof about `name.sem` at a point no consumer checks is not covered by the loader-side guards. | LeanModels/Sv/RangeGuard2.lean header |
| x/z digits inside a casez/casex item EXPRESSION (svGolf gate) | x/z digits are exempt anywhere inside a casez/casex item, not only as the item's own literal; `casez (a[1:0]) (a[0] == 1'bz) ? 2'b00 : 2'b01: ...` passes the gate (svgolf/score/tests/gate/casez_expr.sv). Whether ls-sv and Yosys then differ was not measured. | svgolf/score/srcgate.py (xz_literal_findings); measured by the register authors |

## Data format

- entries[] (ls-sv tier) and svgolf.entries[] (svGolf checker) share one record shape:
- id (unique slug), tag (display name; `Family:detail` where the code has one), group, layers (extractor | lean-model | lean-guard | lean-loader | lean-proof-tooling | svgolf-*), trigger (a measured source, `H:` = the body of the standard test module), why, category (refused-now | later | never | refused-pending), proposed (true = not confirmed by Thomas), decided_by (the recorded decision), since (date, when known).
- later: prerequisite (required) and plan (a plan_items id); never: principle (required, from the principle table); refused-pending: decided_by or source (the decision) and kinds that may be absent from the code.
- svgolf (optional, on an ls-sv entry): {category, principle | prerequisite, proposed}: the status for a svGolf submission when it differs from the ls-sv status.
- kinds.extractor / kinds.lean: the code tags the row covers (exact strings; `glob:<pattern>` for a deliberate family; `@default:<function>` for an extractor site that takes the slang class name; a bare `*` for a site whose whole kind is built at run time). The completeness check requires every live code tag to be covered and every listed tag to exist.
- match: [{file, text}]: for a refusal that has only a message, the text must still be found in the file. where: [{file, fn}]: the function that raises it (line numbers are resolved by --where, never stored). attacks: svgolf only, `task/name` of every tests/expected.json design the row explains.
- evidence (where it is documented), unverified (read from the source, never triggered by a run), verified_by_run, notes, value_rank / value_note (the ordering of the 'Allowed later' table), aggregate (svGolf only: a summary row hidden from svgolf/REFUSALS.md).

## Keeping this file true

`python3 tools/gen_sv_refusals.py --check` fails when the extractor or the Lean code raises a tagged refusal that is not listed here, when a listed tag has disappeared from the code, or when this file is stale. After round-6 style work: rerun `--check`, add the new rows to `docs/sv-refusals.json`, run `--write`. A checkout without `svgolf/` (the svGolf project lives on the golf branch) is checked for this half only: `--check` says it skipped the svGolf half and `--write` regenerates this file alone.
